paper.title: Algorithm 783: Pcp2Nurb -- Smooth free-form surfacing with linearly trimmed bicubic B-splines
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 24(3), 261-267 (TOMS 783, Sep 1998)

code.note: C shell archive (C/Drivers/Sp/). Remove everything above the #! /bin/sh line, run it with sh to create C/ with the Pcp2Nurb sources (src.c, pcp2nurb), driver1.c and driver2.c, and the reference files RES1 and RES2 (Inventor ascii). The driver1.c header says: cc -g -c nurb_iv1.c; cc -g -c pcp2nurb.c; cc -o nurb_iv1 ... -lm; run as 'nurb_iv1 0.5' (default blend ratio). Rebuild the program from the shar's sources; the claim is on the printed output of driver1 with blend 0.5, compared with RES1.

claim.location: The shipped reference output C/Drivers/Sp/RES1 (member of 783.gz): the first Coordinate3 point list, which belongs to the first NurbsSurface (the first patch of the three-patch corner blend). Point 1 of that list is 0.493056 1.868056 0.972222.

reference.file: C/Drivers/Sp/RES1 (member of 783.gz), first Coordinate3 block, point 1

claim.metric: The x, y and z of the first control point of the first NurbsSurface printed by driver1 with blend ratio 0.5, compared with 0.493056, 1.868056, 0.972222 from RES1 (each component, absolute).
claim.paper_value: Not used: the paper is paywalled and was not read.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. RES1 prints 6 decimals (rounding up to 5e-7). The code is single precision (float), so a few-ulp difference per operation on magnitudes near 2 can reach about 1e-6 after a chain of operations; 1e-5 absolute allows that and still resolves to the fifth decimal, far below any change of the algorithm. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 2 minutes: a C compile and one run of driver1.
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text.

why: The shipped RES1 is a printed reference geometry from the Pcp2Nurb driver with fixed default input, so a control point is a checkable number that the code must compute.
